_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never fetched by the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated (formative: automatically when the student clicks Generate; assessed: only via the ?teacher=1-gated action, after Final Submit). markingScheme.criterion: Names the specific item chosen from their own Sort Rush Investigation Record and states which category it was sorted into.
markingScheme.accept: Any genuine item and category from the student's own logged results.
markingScheme.insufficient: A generic answer with no specific item named from their own record.

markingScheme.criterion: Correctly describes what that category of software actually does (System Software runs the whole computer/device; an Application lets you do a specific task; a Utility & Programming Tool keeps the computer safe/running well or is used to write new software).
markingScheme.accept: Equivalent phrasing in the student's own words; exact category wording not required if the meaning is clearly the same job.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains how they could tell the item matched that job — a real feature or behaviour of the item that fits the category's job, not just restating the category name.
markingScheme.insufficient: Simply repeating the category description without linking it back to the specific item.

markingScheme.criterion: Lists three genuinely different programs or apps the student actually uses (not three examples copied from the activity's own teaching content).
markingScheme.insufficient: Fewer than three items, or items copied directly from the Boot Bay/App Spotter/Utility Squad/Code Forge examples rather than the student's own software.

markingScheme.criterion: Assigns a correct category (System Software, Application, or Utility & Programming Tool) to each of the three items listed.
markingScheme.accept: Minor category-naming variation is fine as long as the correct one of the three types is clearly meant.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives a genuine reason for at least two of the three category choices, referring to what that item actually does for the student.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming a category with no reason given, for any of the items.

criteria.source: Auto-marked from the Knowledge Check (auto_marked_score) — the teacher does not mark this row.
= the Explain question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: Does not refer to a specific item from their own Sort Rush results.
Names an item from their own results, but the category's job is described vaguely or incorrectly.
Names an item and correctly describes the category's job, with a small gap in linking the two.
Clearly names their own item, correctly describes the category's job, and explains exactly how the item matched it.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: Does not list three genuine items of their own software, or no categories are given.
Lists three items with categories, but with an incorrect category or no reasons given.
Lists three items with mostly correct categories and at least one genuine reason.
Lists three genuinely different items of their own software, all correctly categorised, with clear reasons for at least two.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks above.

levels.descriptor: Hard to follow, or category names are missing/incorrect throughout.
Understandable, but sentences are unclear or a category name is used incorrectly.
Clear, complete sentences using the correct category names throughout.

markingInstructions: This is a Primary 2 (young primary) student. Mark ONLY the two constructed responses, using each question's point-by-point marking_scheme in marking_context (award each point independently unless it names a dependsOn point, in which case only award it if that earlier point was also awarded) and each point's accept/insufficient wording. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain marking_scheme's 3 points, and reasoning's 3 marks ARE the Apply marking_scheme's 3 points — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set of 3 marks ONCE, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers' clarity, never overlapping with the content marks. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Accept simple, age-appropriate wording and do not penalise spelling unless meaning is unclear. Use the raw Investigation Record (item/yourAnswer/correct rows) to verify any claim the student makes about their own Sort Rush results in the Explain answer. Total is out of 15 (7 auto + 3 + 3 + 2). Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 60 words, in warm and encouraging language suitable for a young child.
